made: node docs/proyecto/pixel/reloj-sheet-make.js, from reloj-set.html (window.RELOJ.E) and the design of El reloj (the orchestrator's p6-spec, section reloj). A new scene: no old scene, no remap.

rules.project: pp-engine.js project(x, y, z) with S 26 and this origin: sx = OX + (x - y) / R2 * S, sy = OY + ((x + y) / R2 * .5 - z * COS) * S, depth d = (x + y) / R2 * COS + z * .5 (R2 = sqrt 2, COS = sqrt 3 / 2); OX = W / 2 + originX = 120, OY = H / 2 + originY = 152. A box is the screen bounding box of its projected corners [floor(min x), floor(min y), ceil(max x) - floor(min x), ceil(max y) - floor(min y)]. screen is the projection rounded to whole pixels
rules.uv: the set is laid out square to the picture: a spot is given in (u, v, z), u across the picture (to the right), v down it (towards the camera), the tower's front at v -2; plaza-base.js's PZ.xy(u, v) = ((u + v) / R2, (v - u) / R2) gives the world x, y (world is that). On the picture sx = OX + u * S = 120 + 26 u, and sy = OY + (v / 2 - z * COS) * S = 152 + 13 v - 22.52 z (one z is 22.52 px up). The picture holds u from -4.62 to 4.62
rules.spot: a spot is a world point of the feet (z 0: the ground; z .4: a stool's top; z .72: the table's cloth; z .8: the cage's stand; z 1.0: the counter's top; z 2.1: the balcony's floor; z 4.3, 2.78, 3.55: on the long hand, a sprite) and, drawn there, a character stands with its feet (the lowest row the sprite draws, outline included) resting on the screen row sy, i.e. the sprite's bottom edge on sy, and its middle column on the column sx (rules.anchor). scale is the frog's: 1 everywhere
rules.anchor: the column of the sprite that is on sx; its feet (its lowest drawn row, outline included) rest on row sy - 1, so its bottom edge is on sy. mkPersona (48 wide): column 24 (KIT.PX), 53 rows drawn standing for a grown-up (a 56-row canvas whose lowest row is empty), 41 for a child; the frog mkCoqui(1) (32 x 27): column 16, drawn rows 1 to 24 (row 25 of the canvas is on sy: his head's top is on row sy - 24); abuela sitting mkAbuelaS (52 x 50): column 17 (her middle) and row 36 (her lap) on (sx, sy), the spot being the stool; a child or a grown-up sitting (mkPersona with sent = 1): column 24 and the lap row, the bottom of the hips: row 16 + 2 t + 3 (t 7 a child: 33; t 11 a grown-up: 41) on (sx, sy); a small thing (the plate, the cage, a prize): its bottom edge on sy, its middle column on sx (the box in the spot); a sign (a card, a square): its top left on the box's corner
rules.view: a view has a zoom (here 1: the 196 x 216 window over the 240 x 216 picture) and x0 = the window's left edge, in whole pixels, 0 to 44. Never a fraction
rules.depth: a spot's depth is the engine's d of its world point; front.plane turns it into the depth of each row of a character
rules.hands: the hands: see hands (the pivot, the lengths, the angle convention)
rules.cards: carta_a, carta_b: two 22 px squares 4 px apart, centred over the frog, their foot 3 px above his head: with the frog's feet on (sx, sy) his head's top row is sy -24 (sy - 24), so both squares have their top at y = sy -49 and end at row sy -28; carta_a's left is sx - 24, carta_b's is sx + 2 (box [x, y, 22, 22]). For the frog at pie2 (sx 132, sy 140): carta_a [108,91,22,22], carta_b [134,91,22,22]
rules.carton: abuela's card: five 14 px squares 2 px apart, the first's top left at screen (26, 92): square i (0 to 4) at x 26 + 16 i, y 92

The window's point is the ground point under its middle column at the picture's middle row

front.how: no list. A character is hidden by every set pixel that is nearer the camera than the character's feet (depth test against the baked depth, with the feet's depth plus 0.3): the awning, the counter, the stands and the tables hide whoever is behind them.
front.plane: for the character's pixel on picture row r (r = 0 at the top): depth(r) = d + (sy - (r + .5)) * tan(30 deg) / S, where d is the spot's depth and sy its screen row; the pixel is hidden where bakedZ[r * 240 + x] > depth(r) + bias (bakedZ: window.DEPTH.z of the set page). The same rule as El mostrador's and El cruce's sheets: the upright plane through the feet
front.sprites: between two sprites the nearer pixel wins: the same depth(r), no bias; two planes within 0.001 are a tie and the later layer is drawn. The hands are sprites on the tower's front: their plane goes through the pivot (the tower's front), so the frog, who stands .02 in front of it at the three places on the long hand, is nearer. The signs (the two time cards, the card of numerals and its beans) are drawn over everything

shadows.at: castShadow(x, y, 0, radius) at the world x, y of the spot, for a character standing on the ground (z 0). The spec gives no radius: these are El mostrador's (frog .45, grown-ups .35, children .28) (open point)
shadows.onSeat: whoever stands or sits above the ground (the balcony, the ladder, a stool, the table, the hand, the counter, the cage's stand, the prize table) casts none: it is not ground (a shadow cast at the pavement under it would show in front of it)

Stand-ins used for size: don Tito, the señor and the vendedor are grown-up men (mkPersona; the vendedor with a paper hat, 4 rows taller than the stand-in's head: his head's top 14 rows are the hat and 10 rows of head), the señora who calls the bingo is a grown-up woman (mkPersona, skirt), abuela sits (mkAbuelaS), Luis and Carmen are the family's children, the frog is mkCoqui(1). The hands, the two time cards, the plate, the cage, the prizes, the card of numerals and its beans are drawn in the preview as plain stand-ins.
